### [86] [Verbalising Model's Computation for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23275)
*Yujing Wang,Yulan He,Wenya Wang,Hanqi Yan*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Current Chain-of-Thought (CoT) verification methods detect reasoning faithfulness from model outputs or static activations, but are limited in explaining how unfaithfulness develops during generation. We introduce VERITAS to verbalise the model's computation: how different reasoning anchors emerge, transfer across layers, and surface in the output. VERITAS adopts the layer-wise Jacobian projection to produce a verbalised account of the model's internal reasoning evolution at each generated CoT token. By training a classifier on the extracted features along the traces, we show that these structured features provide insightful perspectives on how and where reasoning diverges toward unfaithfulness. Experiments on four datasets from FaithCoT-Bench and BonaFide show that VERITAS achieves a significant performance gain over LLM-as-Judge, with a 28.4% gain in balanced accuracy, and an average improvement of 16.0% over activation probing. Further analysis shows VERITAS can be generalised to different datasets and model architectures. Our work shows that verbalising model computation provides a richer and more interpretable lens on CoT faithfulness, moving beyond detection toward a mechanistic understanding of how reasoning fails.

### [87] [Inferring L1 Backgrounds from L2 English with LLM Token Probabilities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23309)
*Ahmet Yavuz Uluslu,Mark Gales,Kate Knill,Gerold Schneider*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Native language identification (NLI) infers a non-native speaker's first language (L1) from their second language (L2) production. We investigate a token probability approach that scores each text sample as a continuation of a prompt prefix specifying a candidate L1, then predicts the candidate with the highest score. We evaluate our approach using Llama 3.1 8B and 70B on three datasets: TOEFL9, Write and Improve 2024, and BULATS-L1. We compare its performance with previous prompting-based classification approaches. Token-probability scoring substantially improves on direct classification, particularly with the 8B model, while the 70B model achieves state-of-the-art performance across all datasets. Our results indicate that pretrained LLMs' token probabilities contain information useful for distinguishing L1 backgrounds from L2 English production.

### [88] [On the Tip of the Tongue: First-Token Cueing as a Behavioral Probe of Recall Failures in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23400)
*Jaewon Sok,Jewon Yeom,Seonghyeon Park,Jeongjae Park,Hwiyeong Lee,Taesup Kim*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models often answer factual questions incorrectly in closed-book settings, and such errors are usually attributed to missing knowledge. Yet models often encode answers they fail to produce. We show that many closed-book errors are first-token recall failures: the model commits to a wrong first token, but once given the right one it completes the answer and often recognizes it as correct. We study this with First-Token Cueing, a behavioral probe that prefills the response with the first token of the gold answer. Model uncertainty peaks at the first answer token, where it already predicts correctness, and among gold prefixes of any length the first token alone accounts for the largest share of recovered errors. Across 16 open models, this one token corrects between a fifth and a half of the errors on multi-token answers in English QA and improves accuracy in all seven languages of a multilingual benchmark. Most of the errors it corrects are also solved by the model's own sampled reasoning, a criterion for encoded knowledge, and models recognize correct starts they do not produce: they continue a correct start more confidently than an incorrect start of the same answer type and prior probability, yet rarely find it without the gold answer. These results locate a recoverable class of factual errors at the first decoding step, where inference-time methods may gain the most.

### [89] [A low-dimensional dynamical basis for tongue shape control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23456)
*Sam Kirkham,Patrycja Strycharczuk*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Speech production involves the control of a high-dimensional articulatory system with many degrees-of-freedom, but a widespread hypothesis is that speakers navigate this complexity using a set of lower-dimensional control variables. Common candidates for these control variables include individual articulators (e.g. tongue body) and abstract tract variables (e.g. tongue body constriction location), but identifying the most appropriate coordinate system for articulatory control remains an open question. In this study, we advance a model in which holistic tongue shape modes represent a potential low-dimensional control basis for a simple dynamical law. We first discover empirical tongue shape modes in a cross-speaker coordinate space and then fit the model to ultrasound data on monophthongal vowels from 36 speakers of British English. A three-dimensional linear point attractor fitted to these time-varying modes recovers the dynamics of tongue shape with a high degree of accuracy. This suggests that complex tongue movement can arise from independent modes that linearly combine under simple dynamical laws, thereby relocating some complexity from the control signal to the coordinate system. We show that this framing explains why one-dimensional articulatory measures can exhibit observable nonlinearities, and hypothesize that shape modes are a plausible kinematic expression of underlying muscle synergies.

### [90] [MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23480)
*Markus Fischer,Jens Meiler,Matthias Elgeti*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Research groups that want a language model grounded in their own literature face a choice between hosted services that receive their unpublished work and self-hosted deployments that keep the data local but give the model no access to the corpus. Munin is an open-source framework for a self-hosted scientific assistant that indexes a group's corpus and its citation graph, and wraps whichever open-weight model the group can serve in an agent harness with specialised reading, search, and computation tools. We claim that the harness, rather than the specific model, is what makes the system useful on domain literature, and we ship the evaluation suite that tests this claim with the software. On 199 paired literature questions, the harness more than doubles the accuracy of the base model, from 0.387 to 0.874 (+0.487, 95% CI [0.407, 0.568]), while naive retrieve-then-answer scores below the unaided model on every backbone tested. Under the harness, roughly twice as many answer claims trace to a passage the model read itself as with fixed top-5 retrieval. When the source paper for a question is removed from the corpus, the system abstains on about nine in ten of the questions it had answered correctly on the Qwen backbones and eight in ten on gpt-oss-20b, and it produces no fabricated local citation across 300 fabricated references. The pattern holds on three backbones from two developers, including a 20-billion-parameter model that runs on a single consumer-grade GPU. With all outbound network access disabled, both Qwen backbones still exceed the published PaperQA2 accuracy. The evaluation suite runs as a single command, so an adopting group can re-run it on its own corpus and model.

### [91] [Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23521)
*Xin Qiu,Junlong Tong,Wei Zhang,Xiaoyu Shen*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) can now perceive, describe, and reason about images and audio, yet time series understanding remains underestimated: most work uses LLMs as forecasters and classifiers, reasoning studies are few and narrow, and no suite trains and evaluates the full range of capabilities. In this paper, we build the first such suite, with 337K training and 44K evaluation samples across three progressive capabilities, Perceive, Solve, and Reason, and use it to ask how time series should enter an LLM that must master all three, and in what order. We find that a dedicated encoder is essential: with one, a 4B model surpasses GPT-4o on every perception attribute we test, whereas textualizing the series costs 8--10 points in reasoning accuracy. The capabilities then build on one another: learning them in order beats mixing the same data and rivals reasoning-only training with over three times the reasoning data, but only when an encoder is used. Analyses further reveal that capabilities are transferred through distinct network depths rather than simply stacked, and that a stage converged on its own benchmark is not necessarily ready for the next. Distilled into a simple recipe, these findings yield 4B TS-LLMs that, without any target-domain data, outperform four recent 7B TS-LLMs on seven of eight out-of-domain metrics, by up to 11 points. We therefore advocate treating time series as a first-class modality for LLMs, read through dedicated encoders and taught to perceive before they reason.

### [92] [EduWild: How Teacher-Configured Chatbots Fail in Real-World Use and How to Fix Them](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23530)
*Ziqi Liu,Ruiwei Xiao,Yuxuan Li,John Stamper*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Teachers increasingly configure educational chatbots through natural-language instructions, but how these bots fail in real-world use remains poorly understood. We introduce EduWild, a dataset of 1,726 conversations with 217 teacher-configured chatbots, each paired with the instructions and configuration behind it, including 900 conversations from the intended end users of 35 deployed chatbots. We develop a 29-code taxonomy covering factual, workflow, diagnostic, and pedagogical failures and apply it using a human-calibrated LLM judge. The most frequent failures are lapses in following teacher intent --- bots skip required workflow steps (53.8% of end-user conversations), omit expectation setup (33.4%), and overload learners with information or questions (37.1%). Guided by these findings, we design a prompt-based harness targeting the six most frequent failure modes. In a study with 200 college students across ten bots, the harness reduces the mean number of target failure codes per conversation from 1.406 to 0.489, a 65.2% relative reduction with bots weighted equally. These findings show how real-world failure analysis can guide practical improvements to educational chatbots.

### [93] [ConvexLLM: Scaling Convex-Hull Speech Interfaces to General-Purpose Audio Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23539)
*Ming-Hao Hsu,Shujie Liu,Yuxuan Hu,Yuxiang Wang,Yingda Shen,Jinyu Li,Zhizheng Wu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Speech and audio language models connect continuous acoustic representations to decoders pretrained primarily on text data. Most such models use MLP or Q-Former interfaces to map acoustic features into the decoder's input space, requiring the decoder to learn how to interpret the resulting representations. We investigate whether grounding these representations in the decoder's existing text embeddings can help it use acoustic information while better preserving its pretrained text capabilities. We present ConvexLLM, a general-purpose speech and audio language model whose C-Gate interface represents audio as continuous convex combinations of frozen text embeddings. ConvexLLM achieves an eleven-task VoiceBench aggregate of 75.36, the highest among the open-weight models we compare, and an MMAU Test-mini accuracy of 62.50%. Its largest margins over the baselines are on spoken knowledge and reasoning tasks, while the strongest baselines are more accurate on audio understanding and transcription. In a comparison with a 2B-parameter decoder, C-Gate achieves higher aggregate spoken-language performance than MLP and Q-Former interfaces, with text-task performance close to MLP and task-dependent tradeoffs in transcription and audio understanding. These results support convex combinations of text embeddings as a viable interface for general-purpose speech and audio language models.

### [94] [MARS: Memory-Aware Routing for Session-Level LLM Assistants](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23583)
*Minghan Wang,Jinhang Zuo,Zhongxiang Dai,Zhiyong Wang,Fang Kong*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Long-term LLM assistants must repeatedly decide what prior context to expose and which model should answer as an interaction evolves. Existing memory systems and model routers usually make these decisions separately, although memory construction changes the evidence, distractors, and difficulty of the resulting input. We introduce MARS, a memory-aware routing framework that uses session state as a shared control interface between memory construction and model selection. A Query and Topic Manager (QTM) estimates compact decision-relevant state that guides a fixed state-conditioned memory policy and an online router, enabling each turn to receive an appropriate memory view and a suitable model under a quality-memory-cost trade-off. We evaluate MARS on RealMem and MultiChallenge with 16 system configurations each, covering long-history memory-driven interaction and bounded sessions with structured context interference. On RealMem, MARS preserves 98.2% of full-context GPT-4o's QA while using only 14.5% of its generation API cost, including both generation and controller calls for MARS, and achieves the strongest measured memory-recall and retrieval scores among compared systems. On MultiChallenge, MARS trails the strongest static system overall but approaches its performance at lower recorded cost on a mechanism-focused subset. Together, these results support a favorable quality-memory-cost trade-off for long-history, memory-dependent interaction.

### [95] [Analyzing Occupational Gender Bias across the LLM Training Lifecycle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23587)
*Manthan Gadhia,Alexander Hoyle,Karolina Stańczak*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Post-training is widely assumed to reduce the social biases language models inherit from pretraining, yet direct evidence for this assumption remains mixed. In this paper, we examine how gender disparities evolve across the language modeling pipeline. In particular, we study occupational gender bias in OLMo 3, a fully open language model family, across its post-training stages by prompting each checkpoint to generate open-ended narratives about synthetic personas given their occupation and education. We consider two settings, a gender-given setting in which the profile states the persona's gender explicitly and a gender-assumed setting in which it must be inferred by the model. We find that when gender is stated, post-training increases semantic diversity for male-coded profiles, whereas for female-coded profiles the increase is smaller after SFT and not significant after DPO and RLVR. When gender is assumed by the model, post-training affects narratives about female and male personas similarly. The model's own gender assumptions, however, show a consistent female-preferential skew relative to United States labor-force demographics, except for heavily male-dominated occupations. Every successive post-training stage monotonically increases the odds of attributing a female label over the base model. A provenance analysis of the supervised fine-tuning corpus finds only a modest 7.7% female-token surplus, too small to explain the size of these downstream effects. The project code is available under: this https URL .

### [96] [In Human Memories. Technology, Creativity and Self-Determination: An Ethical Proposal](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23651)
*Francesco Vitucci,Giuseppe Silvi,Francesco Abbrescia,Anthony Di Furia,Francesco Scagliola*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: This research investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in modern compositional practices, with a particular focus on two case studies: Convergence (2020/21) by Alexander Schubert, for String Ensemble and AI System, and In Human Memories (2024) by Francesco Vitucci, for four cellos and one electroacoustic player, whose installation was created by the Electronic Music School of the "N. Piccinni" Conservatory of Bari. The initial historical survey traces the evolving use of technology in composition, revealing how the search for new expressive possibilities has driven the development of technological tools through experimentation. The appearance of AI marks a fundamental shift: no longer just a tool, AI now poses questions and challenges to the composer. Engaging with AI becomes an exploration of an unknown entity, whose full capabilities are still largely undiscovered. This new interaction leads composers to confront AI not merely as a passive resource but as a participant in the creative process, outlining an ethical path to reclaim technology as a creative tool. In Human Memories reflects this dynamic, demonstrating how AI can serve as both inspiration and a driving force in shaping contemporary music.

### [97] [VISTA: Steering LLMs with Latent User Values Inferred from a Few Survey Answers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23702)
*Yinuo Xu,Jadie Adams,Brian Hu,Shivani Kumar,David Jurgens,Arslan Basharat*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Personalizing a language model requires knowing what a person values, which stays largely consistent across tasks. Yet most methods either learn task-specific preferences or place the user's profile in the prompt, where models struggle to act on it. We introduce VISTA (Value-Informed Steering and Targeted Acquisition), which infers a latent profile from users' (full or partial) survey answers, and maps the profile through a hypernetwork to a user-specific steering intervention in a frozen LLM to select answer choices or generate free-text responses. Given the same evidence, VISTA matches or beats in-context profiles on synthetic preferences (Food2D), the World Values Survey (WVS), and PrimeX, without adding prompt tokens. To reduce the cognitive burden of completing full surveys, VISTA also chooses which questions to ask and when to stop: on WVS it stops after 6% of the questionnaire while retaining 94% of the full-history gain, where standard adaptive testing retains at most 42%. The dominant steering direction is an interpretable value axis on which VISTA places unseen users accurately. Our results point toward pluralistic alignment that adapts to individuals at deployable cost.

### [98] [The Cognitive Cost of LLM Writing: A Reading-Time Comparison with Human Text](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23715)
*Kamer Cekini,Elisabetta Biondi,Chiara Boldrini,Andrea Passarella,Marco Conti*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Although linguistic differences between human-written and Large Language Model (LLM)-generated texts have been extensively studied, their implications for the cognitive effort involved in reading remain less explored. In psycholinguistics, reading time is commonly used as an indirect measure of cognitive processing effort. Building on this perspective, we investigate whether human-written texts and their LLM-generated rewrites exhibit differences in predicted reading time that may reflect differences in processing demands for readers. To this end, we introduce RoBERTa-RT, a model trained on human eye-tracking data to predict word-level reading times. We evaluate the model on both internal and external test sets, construct a paired dataset of 496 human-written articles and their LLM-generated rewrites, and apply RoBERTa-RT to compare their predicted reading times. Our findings show that LLM-generated rewrites tend to be shorter and have slightly lower predicted total reading times, while exhibiting higher predicted reading times per word. These differences are associated with systematic linguistic changes, including longer and less frequent words, greater lexical diversity, and higher contextual predictability. From a cognitive perspective, our findings suggest that LLM-generated writing may redistribute reading demands: reducing the amount of text to process while increasing the predicted processing effort associated with individual words. This highlights the importance of considering not only the linguistic characteristics of machine-generated content, but also its potential implications for human cognitive processing.

### [99] [Recognizing Study Lineage Is Not Enough: Over-Crediting Same-Trial Evidence in LLM-Based Medical Verification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23721)
*Mukand Krishna,Anoushka Harit,Chenghao Xiao,Zhongtian Sun*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Publication count is not study count. A model can identify shared trial lineage correctly in a direct task yet over-credit a second publication from the same trial when aggregating evidence. We evaluate this behavior in medical LLM verification using 14 source-audited clinical families and five model conditions. The families span provenance, clinical applicability, result direction, and composition; the provenance families provide the direct lineage tests. Recognition and aggregation are separate stateless calls, and repeated calls assess within-input stability. Across all three original provenance families, GPT-5.5 identifies the independent update in 10/10 recognition calls per family but over-credits the same-trial report in 5/5 separate aggregation calls per family. Selected Qwen3-4B and Ministral-3-8B conditions show the same cross-task contrast. A study-grouping instruction reduces GPT-5.5 over-credit from 4/5 to 0/5 in each later pure-provenance family. Other model conditions show mixed behavior, and rejected outputs limit several comparisons. The results identify a behavioral gap between elicited lineage recognition and evidence aggregation. The code and data artifacts are available at this https URL .

### [100] [The Italian lawmaking process: a unified and structured dataset](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23741)
*Matilde Contestabile,Chiara Ferrara,Giovanni Parrillo,Lorenzo Emer,Andrea Vandin*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: The Italian legislative process is documented in detailed parliamentary records hosted in institutional websites. However, much of this information is available only as unstructured text, limiting its systematic reuse. We applied a controlled, systematic LLM-based extraction procedure, validated against manually annotated records, to convert these texts into ordered and dated events including, e.g., bill introduction, committee examination, plenary examination, and approval. The resulting dataset reconstructs the procedural histories of all 5346 Italian laws enacted between 1985 and 2026, spanning parliamentary terms IX to XIX, for overall 101413 events. Each event records the activity, date, and chamber, with additional procedural details where available. The dataset supports research in the emerging fields of computational legal and legislative studies, potentially combined with process-oriented data science methods to examine procedural paths and legislative timing across parliamentary terms.

### [101] [DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23787)
*Jiaming Xu,Hanzhen Wang,Tianlang Zhao,Jiewen Xiao,Chengze Yuan,Jiayi Pan,Yongkang Zhou,Jiancai Ye,Yu Wang,Guohao Dai*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Speculative decoding has become a mainstream technique for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate candidate tokens that are subsequently verified by the target model. However, agentic workloads introduce long and continuously evolving contexts and frequent multi-turn interactions. Under such workloads, we observe that existing draft models suffer from up to an 80% degradation in acceptance length, while maintaining their historical KV cache introduces substantial system overhead. In this paper, we identify the growing historical context as a common source of both problems and introduce DLite, a history-free speculative decoding framework for agentic AI. DLite directly reuses contextual hidden states from the target model and performs local speculative prediction without explicitly maintaining the historical context, transforming an increasingly complex modeling problem into local simple prediction problem. A lightweight sequential head further restores intra-block causal dependencies with low overhead. To effectively train this heterogeneous history-free architecture, we introduce a tailored two-stage training strategy. Experiments on general-purpose, long-context and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves 2-6 acceptance length and outperforms the state-of-the-art speculative decoding method, DSpark, up to 70%.

### [102] [Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23807)
*Ailiang Lin,Zhuoyun Li,Yusong Wang,Keyu Mao,Kotaro Funakoshi,Manabu Okumura*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: While deriving text embeddings directly from frozen LLMs has emerged as a promising direction, existing methods focus almost exclusively on English, leaving multilingual settings largely unexplored. In this work, we present the first systematic study of multilingual training-free text embeddings in LLMs. Our analysis reveals a language-conditioned embedding geometry in which semantically equivalent sentences remain misaligned across languages. We hypothesize that language-specific variation can be disentangled from semantic content to improve embedding quality. To this end, we propose Paired-Residual Subspace Removal (PRSR), a training-free inference-time intervention that steers LLM representations toward a more language-invariant semantic space. PRSR first constructs paired residuals from multilingual parallel sentences to capture language-specific deviations. It then estimates layer-wise low-rank subspaces from these residuals and suppresses the corresponding components in the last-token hidden states. We conduct more than 200 monolingual evaluations across 18 languages using MTEB and MMTEB, along with cross-lingual bitext mining between English and over 200 other languages. Empirical results demonstrate that PRSR consistently improves the performance of existing training-free baselines in both monolingual and cross-lingual settings across different LLMs.

### [103] [Acceptance Is Not Speed: Length Inflation in Training-Free Lossy Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23818)
*Chiatzen Wang,Bill Xu,Haochen Gu,Hongyang Zhang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Speculative decoding typically characterizes speedup by draft tokens accepted per verification round. Lossless verification preserves the target model's output distribution and thus expected completion length, making this metric a meaningful efficiency proxy. Relaxed (lossy) verification accepts tokens that lossless verification would reject, potentially altering that distribution. We identify a length inflation phenomenon: relaxed verification lengthens completions, primarily by extending reasoning traces, largely offsetting apparent gains in accepted tokens per round. We evaluate existing training-free relaxed verification rules on twelve target-drafter pairs against lossless verification on identical prompts, measuring completion length, verifier rounds, wall-clock time, and task accuracy. At each rule's most relaxed evaluated setting, relaxed verification on average accepts $1.34\times$ as many tokens per round but produces $1.54\times$ longer completions. For rules with higher acceptance lengths, tokens accepted only under relaxed verification tend to have low target-model probability, contributing to length inflation. For rules that reduce verifier rounds, accuracy typically drops substantially. Further analysis traces some failures to continued reasoning that exhausts the budget needed to deliver a final answer. Overall, accepted tokens per round alone is an unreliable measure of decoding speed under relaxed verification. Completion length and verifier rounds must also be reported to assess actual efficiency.

### [104] [DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23839)
*Jianyuan Zhong,Chenwei Wu,Zhaochen Yu,Xixian Jiang,Xuewei Li,Hao Xiao,Xilin Dai,Junyang Wang,Jiaru Zou,Zhiqing Cui,Boyuan Zheng,Jing Xiong,Zhen Zhang,Qiang Gao,Michael Morley,Luis Nakayama,Qiang Xu,Liyue Shen,Tao Gui,Leo Anthony Celi,James Zou,Zhenfei Yin,Yingcheng Wu,Ling Yang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.

### [105] [A misinformation playbook sharpens judgement without breeding cynicism](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22724)
*Tong Guo,Teng Ye,Yutong Xie,Qiaozhu Mei*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Misinformation harms public health and democracy, and generative artificial intelligence now writes falsehoods as persuasive as people's. Defences range from fact-checking individual claims to training people to resist falsehoods. Yet many claims are too new to check, and interventions that teach doubt can reduce belief in truth too. We propose a defence that targets not the facts of each claim but the persuasion strategies that recur across them. Here we show that learning misinformation's persuasion playbook, mapped from 214,646 fact-checked claims in 51 languages, can sharpen human and machine judgement of claims they know little about, without making either more cynical about true claims. The playbook spans social influence, information manipulation and emotional appeals, combined around a core of fear, conspiracy and fabrication. Briefed with it, plus a reminder that persuasion is not proof of falsehood, a language model better distinguished true from machine-generated false claims about events after its training data. In a pre-registered experiment, the same briefing improved people's discernment of claims they reported as unfamiliar and left their belief in true claims unchanged. Averaged over all claims, the gain was not statistically significant. Because it targets what recurs, this defence need not wait for claim-specific fact-checks.

### [106] [Can AI interview? Comparing AI-led to Human-led Chat Interviews](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23149)
*Semra Guven,Tobias Gårdhus,Andreas Bjerre-Nielsen,Anna Rogers,Hjalmar Bang Carlsen*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Large language model chatbots have been proposed as AI-interviewers for collecting qualitative interview data at scale, potentially bridging social science's longstanding divide between the breadth of surveys and the depth of qualitative interviews. This paper provides the first direct empirical comparison of data quality in AI-led and human-led interviews. In a randomized experiment (N = 41), university students were interviewed via synchronous text chat by either trained non-expert interviewers or a locally hosted AI system; we evaluate exposure, specificity, and relevance. Median interview duration was similar across conditions, but AI-interviewers asked more than twice as many questions per interview and elicited roughly 65 percent more respondent text per interview. Per-question responses were longer with human interviewers, though not after multiple-testing correction; only AI-condition participants skipped questions. Responses were almost uniformly on-topic in both conditions; for specificity we detect no difference, but the design cannot exclude one of up to three quarters of a point. These results were obtained with a small, locally hosted open-weight model (7B parameters), which addresses concerns about data security, GDPR compliance, and scientific reproducibility. Our findings support the viability of AI-interviewing for large-N qualitative data collection.

### [107] [Social Bias or Social Desirability? Comparing Factorial Survey Experiments for Humans and Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22409)
*Franziska Weeber,Thomas Hinz,Konstantin Mozer,Sam Sievers,Alan Akbik,Sebastian Padó*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Factorial survey experiments are a survey method from the social sciences that uses descriptions of socially complex situation (``vignettes'') to elicit judgments such as social bias. They provide two major benefits: (a), they reduce the effect of social desirability inherent in self-reported social biases, and (b), they make it possible to separate the effects of multiple sociodemographic attributes. These aspects are also desiderata for the evaluation of social bias in LLMs, but are often ignored in social bias evaluations. In our study, we evaluate social bias in humans and eleven LLMs on the basis of four different English and German factorial survey experiments. Our results show that the LLMs mirror the human biases only partially and sometimes even invert them. We provide evidence that this is due to a fundamental difference in how humans and LLMs react to socially complex situations. While such vignettes reduce social desirability bias in humans, this is not the case for LLMs, where the alignment-induced tendency towards socially desirable responses carries over directly. We therefore caution against applying bias measurement techniques from the social sciences that were developed for human to measure attitudes and bias in LLMs.

### [108] [Beyond What Is Visible: Context-Aware Sentiment Across Online Communities Among Crisis Events](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22551)
*Zihui Ma,Yiheng Chen,Lingyao Li,Chen Chen,Fan Yang,Xiao Huang,Haozheng Liu,Yuhan Wang,Runlong Yu,Gregory B. Baecher*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Social media offers timely insight into disaster experiences, yet online communities may not represent those affected on the ground. Uneven participation can bias crisis information systems toward data-rich locations and obscure communities with fewer digital traces. We address this with an adaptive cross-community learning framework that combines text and aggregate mobility signals with socioeconomic and hazard-informed community representations, supplementing sparse local observations with evidence from structurally related cities. We evaluate the framework on the January 2025 Southern California wildfires and 2024 Hurricane Helene in Florida. The adaptive model achieves the highest F1-score in both cases (0.5923 and 0.7615), while augmentation has its strongest effect where original observations are limited. The framework also reveals finer cross-city community-level sentiment variation and stronger sentiment-mobility correspondence than text-only models, with relationships differing across disaster contexts. These findings support crisis systems that better account for context-dependent evidence and improve interpretation of underrepresented community signals.

### [109] [Generative AI Produces and Transmits Beauty Bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22553)
*AJ Alvero,Deepak Varuvel Dennison,Alexandra Crespin,Heeyon Kim,Alejandra Regla-Vargas,Avani Akerkar,Jasmine McNealy,René Kizilcec*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Societies reward people judged to be attractive by standards intertwined with gender and race. In this paper, we examine if and how generative AI may contribute to these dynamics. We audited 27 text-to-image generators released between 2022 and 2026 using simple prompts that never mention attractiveness or beauty, analyzing 51,300 generated faces and 160,196 photographs of real people across primary and supplementary comparisons. We used three automated measures and collected ratings from 550 human raters on a subset of images. Nearly all generators produced faces scoring above photographed faces under automated measures, and human raters judged the outputs of all 23 generators as significantly more attractive than photographed faces, even after correction for multiple comparisons. When focusing our analysis on gender, we find that 37% of female-prompted generated faces outscored the median professional fashion model. Across racial, ethnic, and national categories, groups associated with darker skin tones tended to receive lower attractiveness scores than groups associated with lighter skin tones. In a preregistered hiring simulation experiment (N = 570), exposure to AI-generated faces selected for high human-rated attractiveness lowered hireability and trustworthiness ratings and reduced interview advancement for an identical test set of candidates paired with photographs of real people; exposure to retouched photographs produced no such effect. Generative AI can reproduce racial hierarchies and gendered patterns of beauty and alter the context in which real people are judged.

### [110] [Regulating for an AI Commons: Adopting, sustaining, and defending people-first innovation trajectories](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23212)
*Abhineet Nayyar,Mallory Knodel,Kimberlee Weatherall,Gunn Jiravuttipong*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Technological principles of openness, interoperability, and decentralization are integral to building an AI economy that is accountable to the public and truly responsive to local needs and constraints. However, Big Tech's firm control over essential elements of the stack (such as chips, cloud, models, data, and talent) limits valuable alternatives from reaching the scale necessary for sustained growth. Worse still, hyperscalers continue to enclose and extract value from publicly funded and volunteer-driven technologies without adequately distributing these returns. We see consolidated power within a few entities and "enshittification" of once-transformative innovations. Embedding ethical micro-level tools (like open data repositories or small-language models) into workflows is promising, but without a consistent innovation strategy, they also often end up perpetuating and being appropriated by the same exploitative trajectories. Instead, this whitepaper outlines a three-pillared holistic and intentional policy approach that i) actively pushes for the adoption of cooperative technologies in existing and emerging systems, ii) sets up collective institutional structures to sustain and maintain them in the long-term, and iii) introduces regulatory proposals that limit private entities from disempowering them through uncontrolled enclosure and extraction. Through desk research and purpose-specific case studies, we argue for the importance of such an approach in the Global South, where structural constraints around infrastructure, financing, and policy governance make it difficult for AI commons and cooperative AI tools to emerge and survive. The paper concludes with key open questions for campaigners, policy advocates, researchers, and grassroots organizers to consider and explore while working towards peoples' solidarity within and between Global South countries.

### [111] [Evaluating Predictor-Corrector Dependence in Hard-Constrained Climate Emulators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23561)
*Tianyu Zhang,Xinyu Wang,Zhenghan Tai,Xiao-Wen Chang,Yoshua Bengio*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Climate emulators often enforce physical constraints by correcting each state predicted by a neural network, but evaluating only the corrected forecast conflates predictor skill with the effect of the correction. We introduce an evaluation framework that separates these contributions by comparing corrected forecasts, pre-correction predictions along corrected trajectories, and autonomous rollouts with correction disabled. We further cross correction during training and inference to distinguish its immediate effect from how it shapes the learned predictor, and use matched nonphysical controls to test whether improvements are specific to the physical correction. In ACE2, correction substantially improves physical consistency. In a three-seed ACE2 pilot, models trained with correction produce less accurate uncorrected precipitation forecasts at short horizons than models trained without correction, but more accurate forecasts at 10 and 30 days. This contradicts our preregistered hypothesis that the deficit would grow with forecast horizon. In a separate nine-seed experiment, directly supervising the uncorrected output reverses its precipitation forecast deficit at 72 hours while maintaining the accuracy of corrected forecasts at 24 hours. In ConCerNet's heat-equation system, projection-trained models have higher uncorrected trajectory-based vector-field RMSE than models trained without projection, while restoring the physical projection recovers accuracy far more effectively than a matched nonphysical control. Together, these results show that hard corrections can reshape the predictors trained alongside them, creating dependencies that are not visible from corrected forecasts alone. Hard-constrained emulators should therefore be evaluated by separately measuring predictor accuracy, correction effects, and their interaction during training.

### [112] [GCAM-Gym: A Benchmark for Agent-Based Climate Policy Search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23569)
*Tianyu Zhang,Zhenghan Tai,Xinyu Wang,Irina Rish,Yoshua Bengio*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Comparing climate-policy search methods requires accounting for differences in policy control, available observations, feedback timing, and simulator budgets. We introduce GCAM-Gym, a Gymnasium-compatible environment that supports full-policy evaluation and stepwise control through a common interface and exposes the components of the policy objective. We compare seven search and control systems in three settings: target attainment and cost, cost-temperature trade-offs, and one-step delayed feedback. Each system is evaluated with ten seeds per setting, for a total of 3,210 attempted GCAM evaluations. Four systems share a budget of 24 attempts per seed; among these, CMA-ES achieves the highest interquartile mean (IQM) of the best returns from completed policy evaluations in all three settings. We release the evaluation archive and analysis tools to reconstruct the reported comparisons without running GCAM.

### [113] [Water-Energy-Data nexus reveals sustainability gaps and priorities for AI infrastructure](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23614)
*Jincheng Huang,Guoan Xiao,Xin Lan,Caichun Yin,Zhimeng Jiang,Yue Cui,Jianguo Liu*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) depends on interconnected water, energy, and data systems spanning infrastructure life cycles and diverse geographies, with the potential to intensify water and energy insecurity, exacerbate social inequities and lead to cascading sustainability issues globally. Yet assessments commonly examine them separately, limiting our understanding of where resource pressures arise, how they are transferred across space, and who bears their consequences. To address these challenges, we established a water-energy-data (WED) nexus framework that captures the spatial and life-cycle dependencies of AI infrastructure, and use large language models to synthesize 12,825 water- or energy-related studies across four resource-intensive AI infrastructure activities: mineral extraction, semiconductor manufacturing, data center operation and electronic-waste processing. The evidence map identifies a mismatch between the interconnected activities supporting AI infrastructure and boundaries used to assess them. Researchers assess operational energy more than water use and other indirect demands, while interactions across locations and life-cycle activities remain understudied. These gaps obscure how resource demands shift among infrastructure nodes and regions, and how data-enabled benefits compare with their underlying costs. The WED nexus provides a foundation for integrated assessment of spatially metacoupled systems, while the evidence map can inform priorities for managing the sustainability implications of the AI boom.

### [114] [A Large Language Model LLM Approach to COVID-19 Fake News Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23800)
*Muhammad Arif,Samah Fodeh-Jarad,Elyas Irankhah,Uroosa Fatima,Lama Ayash,Sreeraj Ramachandran*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Text classification is a widely studied problem in information retrieval and data mining, with applications ranging from healthcare diagnosis to the detection of COVID-19-related fake news. Social media platforms generate vast volumes of user-generated text, and the rapid spread of misinformation during the pandemic has made automated fake news detection an important task. In this study, we apply pretrained transformer-based transfer learning (TL) models and large language models (LLMs), namely BERT-base, ALBERT-base, XLM-RoBERTa-base, DistilBERT, GPT-2, XLNet, and T5, to the COVID-19 English Tweets dataset, which contains 6,420 tweets labeled as real or fake. To further improve performance, we apply six late-fusion optimization techniques: weighted fusion, particle swarm optimization (PSO) fusion, the Nelder-Mead algorithm, Powell's method, the Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) algorithm, and trust-region constrained optimization. Models are evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, and confusion-matrix heatmaps are used to visualize the predictions of each model. GPT-2 achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 0.9631, precision of 0.9612, recall of 0.9610, and F1-score of 0.9600, while Nelder-Mead fusion achieved the best result among the fusion methods with an accuracy of 0.9610. These results highlight the value of LLMs for COVID-19 fake news detection. We conclude by outlining future directions, including multiclass classification, multilingual datasets, and real-time social media streams.

### [115] [Hard Instances on Demand](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22637)
*Jamie Fravel,Martin Koutecký,Pavlo Tsitsei*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: 提出将实例生成视为黑盒优化问题，利用Nevergrad平台搜索使求解器运行时间最大化的困难实例，并在SAT、TSP、Hamilton圈、非置换流水车间四个NP难问题上验证其有效性，演化得到的困难实例在多数情况下优于随机实例且与长期策展的基准测试集相媲美。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 随机实例常被用于评估算法，但其结构可能不能反映真实难度；精心策展的基准库需要数十年积累，新问题往往缺乏此类资源。需要一种通用方法自动生成针对特定求解器的困难实例，以补充现有评估手段。

Method: 将困难实例生成转化为黑盒优化问题：对实例空间参数化，以求解器运行时间为目标函数，使用Nevergrad平台（筛选20种优化器后再升级预算）在编码后的box空间内搜索最优（最困难）实例，方法通用且只需求解器、实例编码器和计算预算三个组件。

Result: 在SAT问题上冠军实例对三求解器组合比预算匹配随机采样困难26倍，超过78%的SAT竞赛公式；在TSP问题上20城市的冠军比229城市的TSPLIB最困难实例还难数倍；在NPFS问题上10×5冠军需要CP Optimizer 238.6秒证明最优性，比10万次随机采样中最难实例还慢53倍。优化器还能从运行时间中恢复已知结构（如SAT子句/变量比接近相变点）。

Conclusion: 该方法为实验性论文提供了一个具体默认建议：在报告标准基准性能的同时，应报告固定预算对抗性搜索找到的最困难实例。整个流程负担较轻（每个问题几百到几千CPU小时），且可大规模并行，应作为算法实验的标准组成部分。

Abstract: The conclusions of an experimental study of algorithms are only as good as the instances they are run on. Benchmark libraries for well-studied problems took decades to curate, while evaluations of new problems often fall back on random instances, which are known to be misleading: they may say more about the random generator than about the algorithmic question at hand. We treat instance generation as an optimization problem: parameterize the instance space, take the solver's running time as the objective, and let a black-box optimizer search for hard instances. We develop a widely applicable workflow built on the Nevergrad optimization platform and demonstrate it on four NP-hard problems: satisfiability, traveling salesperson, Hamiltonian cycle, and non-permutation flow-shop scheduling. The search needs only the solver, an instance encoder, and a compute budget. Our evolved instances beat the hardest instance of a budget-matched random draw in all four case studies, by an order of magnitude or more in three. They are often competitive with long-curated benchmark sets: our SAT champion is harder (for a three-solver portfolio) than 78% of the 498 SAT Competition formulas in its size class; our 20-city TSP champions take several times longer than the hardest measured classical TSPLIB instance (229 cities); and our flow-shop champion takes 238.6 seconds of CP Optimizer time to solve to proven optimality (versus 4.5 seconds for the hardest of 100,000 random draws) while denying CP-SAT an optimality proof. The optimizer even recovers known structure from running time alone: it locates a SAT clause/variable ratio near the phase transition and finds structurally different champions for the two scheduling engines.

</details>


### [116] [An improved randomized algorithm for finding sinks of Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations of the binary hypercube](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22546)
*Thomas Dueholm Hansen,Uri Zwick*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations (AUSOs) of the binary hypercube form an elegant abstraction of various optimization problems, ranging from linear programs whose feasibility region is a combinatorial hypercube, to 2-player turn-based stochastic games (2TBSGs) in which one of the players has two actions from each one of its states. The currently fastest known randomized algorithm for finding the sink of such AUSOs is the Random-Facet algorithm of Kalai (STOC 1992), and of Matoušek, Sharir and Welzl (SoCG 1992), adapted to the binary hypercube by Gärtner (RSA 2002). The expected number of vertex queries made by the algorithm is at most $e^{2\sqrt{n}}$, where $n$ is the dimension of the cube. We design an improved randomized sink-finding algorithm that performs an expected number of only $e^{\sqrt{(2+o(1))n}}$ queries. This is the first improved bound for the problem in over two decades. The improved algorithm is obtained by adapting improved versions of the Random-Facet algorithm for solving general linear programs, and LP-type problems, developed by Kalai (STOC 1992), Gärtner (FOCS 1992), and by Hansen and Zwick (STOC 2015). The improved bound is not implied by these much more general algorithms. A key feature of the improved algorithm and its analysis is its simplicity. The structure of binary AUSOs enables a simpler description and a much simpler analysis of the adapted algorithm. In particular, the recurrence relations bounding the complexity of the algorithm depend on only one variable, and not two, and they can be solved using fairly straightforward techniques.

### [117] [Improved Pass Complexity for Semi-Streaming Matching in General Graphs via Budgeted Price Approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22718)
*Tatsuya Terao*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We present a simple deterministic semi-streaming algorithm that computes a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate maximum matching in general graphs in $O(1/\varepsilon^{2})$ passes. This matches the pass complexity of the auction algorithm of Assadi, Liu, and Tarjan~[SOSA'21] for bipartite graphs, and answers Open Question~2 of Assadi~[SOSA'24 \& TheoretiCS'25]. Our approach, which we call the \emph{budgeted price approach}, is very different from the previous $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$-pass semi-streaming algorithms for $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation of matching in general graphs and improves their pass complexity. All previous approaches are augmenting-path-based and use $O(1/\varepsilon^{19})$ passes by Fischer, Mitrović, and Uitto~[STOC'22], $O(1/\varepsilon^{6})$ passes by Mitrović, Mukherjee, Sankowski, and Sheu~[ICALP'25], and $O(1/\varepsilon^{4})$ passes by Izumi, Kitamura, and Yamaguchi~['25].

### [118] [Competitive Online Clustering with Movement Cost](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22824)
*Christian Coester,Yichen Huang,Michael Mitzenmacher*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study the problem of online clustering with movement cost, which generalizes the fundamental $k$-server problem. At each time step, the algorithm is given a set of points in a metric space and must choose $k$ cluster centers. The cost incurred is the sum of the clustering cost at each time step and the total distance that the centers move over time. Prior work established competitive algorithms for the case $k\in\{1,2\}$ on the line metric with the $k$-median clustering objective; under the $k$-median objective, this problem is also known as facility reallocation. We substantially generalize these results to arbitrary $k$, general metric spaces, and a broad class of clustering objectives. Specifically, we consider clustering costs defined as a norm of the distance vector from points to their nearest center, which subsumes the $k$-median, $k$-center, and (square root of) $k$-means objectives, and provide an asymptotically optimal $O(k)$-competitive randomized algorithm against adaptive online adversaries. The algorithm is based on a reduction to the $k$-server problem, establishing a tight connection between the problems. In this reduction, $k$-server requests are generated by Poisson processes, whose arrival rates evolve in continuous time and are driven by a dual representation of the clustering costs. Our method of using Poissonization in this context may also be of independent interest. We demonstrate another use of the idea by deriving similar reductions for batched set chasing problems. We also consider a different family of clustering objectives defined as a norm of the vector of cluster radii, which subsumes the sum-$k$-radii and the $k$-center objectives, and give a tight $O(k)$-competitive deterministic algorithm on the line.

### [119] [On the Metric Distortion of the Minimum Spanning Tree Problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23032)
*Kian Ghassemi,Masoud Seddighin,Saeed Seddighin*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study the metric distortion of the minimum spanning tree (MST) problem when numerical edge weights are unavailable and each vertex reports only a ranking of the other vertices induced by these weights. We first show, through a simple example, that without assumptions on the weights, no ordinal algorithm guarantees a finite approximation ratio. We therefore focus on general metrics and present a Borůvka-inspired algorithm using only ordinal comparisons that achieves distortion $O(\log n)$. We complement this result by showing that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, no deterministic ordinal algorithm guarantees distortion at most $3/2-\varepsilon$ on all finite metric instances. We then investigate more informative settings in pursuit of constant distortion, first considering two well-studied metric classes. For tree metrics realized on the given vertex set, a more careful variant of our initial algorithm achieves distortion~$1$, recovering an optimal MST from ordinal information alone. For the broad class of doubling metrics, a different algorithm based on \emph{endpoint cut stability} achieves distortion $2^{O(D)}$, where $D$ is the doubling dimension; this is constant for fixed $D$, independently of $n$. Finally, we study a query-based extension allowing comparisons between two edge lengths without revealing their numerical values. For general metrics with $n\geq2$, fewer than $n$ edge-comparison queries suffice to achieve distortion at most $2\log_2^* n-1$, which is near-constant even for very large inputs.

### [120] [Online geometric matching and segments block points](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23130)
*Yaqiao Li,Junyi Lin*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Given a sequence of online points in general position in the plane, the geometric matching problem asks to match as many points as possible, subject to segment crossing constraints. We initiate the study of online geometric matching with limited crosses. In the $k$-crossing model each matched segment is allowed to have at most $k$ crosses, where $k=0$ corresponds to the online noncrossing matching model for which Bose et al. proved that Greedy is an optimal deterministic algorithm achieving a competitive ratio of $2/3$. In the triangle-free-crossing model no three matched segments are allowed to pairwise cross each other. Interestingly, we show in both cases the performance of Greedy does not improve by allowing crosses, and in fact, becomes worse in the $k$-crossing setting for $k\ge 1$. In the triangle-free-crossing model, we propose a simple two-layer-Greedy deterministic algorithm achieving a competitive ratio $4/5$. More interestingly, we propose and study the underlying segments blocking points extremal problem, and discuss its connection to vertex cover numbers and Ramsey numbers, with interesting open problems that might be of independent interest. We revisit the noncrossing model. We give a randomized algorithm which is an asymmetric version of Kamali et al., improving the competitive ratio from $0.66952$ to $0.67034$. We also show, via a conceptually simple construction, that no randomized algorithm can match more than $6/7$ fraction of points, improving the previous $16/17$ by Boyar et al.

### [121] [Critical-state algorithms for lot sizing with all-units discounts and variable inventory bounds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23253)
*Kleitos Papadopoulos*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study deterministic single-item lot sizing with all-units quantity discounts, linear holding costs, and time-varying end-of-period inventory bounds. Unit prices may vary arbitrarily over time. For one common positive discount threshold, we give an exact algorithm requiring $O(n^3)$ arithmetic operations and $O(n^2)$ working space, including recovery of an optimal purchase plan. The method combines a critical-state theorem in cumulative-purchase coordinates with two prefix-minimum scans per dynamic-programming layer. The structural argument accommodates downward price discontinuities and distinguishes prescribed from free terminal inventory. With a fixed global set of $m$ positive threshold values, the bounds become $O_m(n^{m+2})$ time and $O_m(n^{m+1})$ space. Period-specific thresholds admit the same exact construction, but its state set can be exponential. For commensurate flow data, an inventory-lattice implementation takes $O(PW)$ time, where $P$ is the total number of price tiers and $W$ is the largest inventory-lattice width. We also derive a conditional optimality certificate from a monotone one-threshold relaxation; this certificate does not imply a near-linear worst-case algorithm for arbitrary prices. Exact-arithmetic implementations are checked against exhaustive inventory dynamic programs and tier-enumeration linear programs. An illustrative timing study identifies settings in which the lattice implementation is preferable.

### [122] [Simpler Algorithms for Capacitated $k$-Median with $(1 + ε)$-Violations Using New Inequalities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23348)
*Han Dai,Shi Li*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We revisit the capacitated $k$-median problem, focusing on constant-factor approximation algorithms with either $(1+\epsilon)$-cardinality or capacity violations. Previous results [DemirciL16, Li16} achieve an $O_\epsilon(1)$-approximation with $(1+\epsilon)$-violations via complex extended configuration linear programming formulations with the round-or-cut framework. We propose a simpler, unified round-or-cut framework that handles both cardinality and capacity violation settings. Our main technical contribution is a mechanism that directly utilizes the costs of local instances to generate valid inequalities. Specifically, we partition the metric space into local pieces of size $O(1/\epsilon)$ as in previous work, and construct instances of capacitated clustering with penalties, which allow client demands to be unserved at a penalty cost. Solving these local instances yields lower bounds on the original LP cost, yielding valid LP constraints. In contrast, previous approaches rely on complex extended configuration LPs over connection variables $x_{ij}$'s and opening variables $y_i$'s. As a secondary contribution, our approach achieves an improved running time of $\text{poly}(n, 1/\epsilon)$, bypassing the exponential dependence on $1/\epsilon$ required to solve the previous extended configuration LPs. Instead of solving the local instances optimally in time exponential in $1/\epsilon$, we obtain $O(1/\epsilon)$-approximate solutions in $\text{poly}(n, 1/\epsilon)$ time. Finally, for the cardinality-violation setting, our algorithm opens a set of at most $(1+\epsilon)k$ $\textit{distinct}$ facilities, and thus gives a bicriteria approximation in the $\textit{hard-capacitated}$ setting. In contrast, the algorithm of [Li16] may open the same facility multiple times.

### [123] [Power of Conditional Sampling on Hypergraphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23364)
*Debarshi Chanda,Buddha Dev Das,Arijit Ghosh,Gopinath Mishra*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a $d$-uniform hypergraph with $|V|=n$ and $|E|=m$. Estimating $m$ from uniformly random hyperedge samples requires $\Theta(\sqrt{m})$ samples by a birthday-paradox argument. We investigate the power of conditional sampling through a hierarchy of oracles: for an integer $1\le s\le d$, given pairwise disjoint subsets $X_1,\ldots,X_s\subseteq V$, the $s$-colorful oracle returns a hyperedge chosen uniformly at random from all hyperedges contained in $X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_s$ that intersect every $X_i$, provided one exists. For $s=1$, this samples a uniformly random hyperedge induced by $X_1$. For every $1\le s\le d$, we give a randomized algorithm that outputs $\widehat{m}\in[(1-\varepsilon)m,(1+\varepsilon)m]$ with probability at least $2/3$ using $O_{s,d}(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon,\log n))$ conditional samples, where the exponent of $\log n$ is an absolute constant independent of both $s$ and $d$. Conditional sampling thus yields an exponential separation over uniform hyperedge sampling. We also study the decision version, in which the oracle only reports whether a qualifying hyperedge exists. For every $1\le s<d$, we prove that any algorithm using the $s$-colorful decision oracle requires $\widetilde{\Omega}_{s,d}(n^{\frac{d-s}{d-s+1}})$ queries. Hence, for $s<d$, access to uniformly random witness hyperedges (random certificates) is exponentially more powerful than existence queries. For $s=d$, decision queries alone achieve $\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon,\log n)$ query complexity, but the exponent of $\log n$ is known to be $\Theta(d)$. The colorful hierarchy thus exhibits a phase transition at $s=d$: for $s<d$, random certificates are essential for polylogarithmic-query estimation, whereas at $s=d$ decision queries suffice, yet random certificates still provably reduce the exponent of $\log n$ from $\Theta(d)$ to an absolute constant.

### [124] [Deterministic Global Minimum Cut Using $\tilde{O}(n^{3/2})$ Cut Queries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23461)
*Yotam Kenneth-Mordoch*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Finding a global minimum cut in an unweighted graph is a fundamental task in the cut-query model. While there exists a randomized algorithm for this task using $\tilde O(n)$ queries, known deterministic algorithms use $\tilde{O}(n^{5/3})$ queries. We improve upon this result and give a simple deterministic algorithm that finds a global minimum cut using $\tilde O(\min\left\{ n\delta,n^2/\delta \right\})$ cut queries, which equals $\tilde{O}(n^{3/2})$ in the worst case, where $\delta$ is the minimum degree of the graph. The key ingredient in our approach is an efficient maximum $s,t$-flow algorithm, for the case when the minimum $s,t$-cut has value at most $\delta$.

Abstract: Finding a global minimum cut in an unweighted graph is a fundamental task in the cut-query model. While there exists a randomized algorithm for this task using $\tilde O(n)$ queries, known deterministic algorithms use $\tilde{O}(n^{5/3})$ queries. We improve upon this result and give a simple deterministic algorithm that finds a global minimum cut using $\tilde O(\min\left\{ n\delta,n^2/\delta \right\})$ cut queries, which equals $\tilde{O}(n^{3/2})$ in the worst case, where $\delta$ is the minimum degree of the graph. The key ingredient in our approach is an efficient maximum $s,t$-flow algorithm, for the case when the minimum $s,t$-cut has value at most $\delta$.

</details>


### [125] [Approximating the Girth of an Undirected, Weighted Graph for Larger Approximation Factors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23698)
*Eliyahu Yablon*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: The girth of a weighted undirected graph is defined as the length of a shortest cycle in the graph. In this paper, we give a randomized $O\left(m^{1+2/(k-1)} n^{1/(k-1)}\right)$ algorithm to approximate the girth of a graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges to within a factor of $k$ for any real $k$. We assume that all edge weights are non-negative. For sufficiently high approximation factors, our algorithm outperforms the state of the art by polylogarithmic factors. Specifically, for approximation factors $k = c\frac{\log n}{\log \log n}$ where $c>5$, our algorithm gives a runtime of $O\left(m (\log n)^{5/c}\right)$, while instantiating the previous best $k$-approximation algorithms with $k = c\frac{\log n}{\log \log n}$ yields a running time of $O\left( \frac{cn (\log n)^{2 + 4/(3c)} }{\log \log n} + m\log n\right)$ (Kadria, Roditty, and Vassilevska Williams, arXiv:2607.00938 ). Furthermore, the algorithm presented here is conceptually simple, has relatively small constants, eschews single-source shortest path and sparse spanner algorithms, and employs a new technique, which we call ``random filtering.'' That being said, the basic algorithm returns only a numerical estimate for the girth, rather than a witness cycle.

### [126] [Dynamic Load Balancing under Restricting Updates](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23768)
*Aaron Bernstein,Sayan Bhattacharya,Peter Kiss,Thatchaphol Saranurak*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study the problem of load balancing in the dynamic setting. The input is a bipartite graph $G = (J \cup M, E)$ of jobs $J$ and machines $M$. Every job has a positive weight $w(j)$. The goal is to assign every job in $J$ to an adjacent machine in $M$ so as to minimize the maximum machine load, where the load of a machine is the sum of the weights of the jobs assigned to it. Although load balancing has been studied extensively in many models of computation, the only previous result in the dynamic model addresses the \emph{incremental} setting, where updates take the form of edge insertions and job deletions [BKS23b]. The authors show a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation for incremental \emph{fractional} load balancing with $\text{poly}(\log(n),1/\epsilon)$ update time; they point out that their techniques do not extend to the decremental setting. Main Result: We obtain an algorithm which maintains a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximate solution to the fractional load balancing problem under edge deletions and job insertions in $\tilde{O}(\log (n), 1/\epsilon)$ update time. Our techniques are very different from those of the incremental algorithm of [BKS23b]. Instead, our algorithm is inspired by a load-balancing algorithm from the {\sc congest} model of computation [ALPZ21]. We develop a novel analytic framework for this algorithm, which allows us to show that it performs well in the dynamic setting. Rounding Scheme: We also present a black-box rounding scheme for dynamic load balancing. Plugging in our fractional algorithm, we obtain a decremental algorithm for $(2+\epsilon)$-approximate \emph{integral} load balancing with $\text{poly}(\log(n),1/\epsilon)$ update time. We also obtain the same bounds for incremental load balancing by plugging in the fractional algorithm of [BKS23b].

### [127] [Polytope Sampling at the Speed of Isoperimetry](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23775)
*Anming Gu,Bobby Shi,Kevin Tian,Hubert Yang*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We give faster algorithms for sampling from the uniform distribution over a polytope. Our main result is an algorithm that, when applied to a polytope with $m$ constraints in $n$ dimensions, uses $m \cdot \mathrm{poly}\log(\frac m \delta)$ iterations, each running in time $O(mn^{\omega - 1})$, to return a sample within total variation distance $\delta$ to the uniform distribution. When $m =O(n)$ and $\delta = \mathrm{poly}(\frac 1 n)$, our runtime improves upon all prior works by an $\Omega(n^{2/3})$ factor. Our sampler is based on the recent \emph{functional stochastic localization} framework of [GST26], and achieves an iteration count nearly matching the Poincaré constant of the uniform distribution with respect to the logarithmic barrier.

### [128] [Online Graph Coloring with Random Arrivals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23824)
*Hirotaka Yoneda,Masataka Yoneda*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study online graph coloring in the random-arrival model, where the vertices are presented in a uniformly random order. Assuming $n$ and $k$ are known in advance, we present a randomized exponential-time algorithm that colors any $k$-colorable graph on $n$ vertices with $O(k^3 \log^2 k \log^4 n)$ colors in expectation. This is the first online coloring algorithm that uses a polylogarithmic number of colors for all fixed $k \geq 3$, and is better than a known lower bound of $\Omega(\log^{k-1} n)$ colors under adversarial arrivals for all fixed $k \geq 6$. In addition, assuming $n$ is known in advance, we obtain a competitive ratio of $\widetilde{O}(n^{2/3})$. For comparison, it is known to be NP-hard to approximate (offline) graph coloring within a factor of $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for all fixed $\varepsilon > 0$. Therefore, our exponential-time online algorithm achieves a performance guarantee beyond the NP-hardness threshold for polynomial-time approximation algorithms.

### [129] [Reusing Calibration Gains across Model Representations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22771)
*Xu Cao,Wenxuan Xiao*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: 本文研究如何将一个模型表征上学到的标定增益（scale calibration gains）迁移到同一预训练模型的另一种表征上（如浮点与GPTQ INT3之间），无需在接收端重新优化。结果表明，迁移可保留76.9%-90.5%的自标定收益，且群组级对应关系和周围网络配置均对迁移效果有影响。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 量化模型标定后可显著改善预测效果，但标定过程需在每个表征上单独执行。研究动机在于：能否将一个表征上学到的增益直接迁移到同一预训练模型的另一表征上，从而避免重复优化并节省成本。

Method: 使用无量纲、逐群组的正增益作为共享接口。浮点模型的增益为exp(θ)的最终值；量化模型的增益通过最终scale与初始scale之比提取。迁移时将增益安装到接收端的权重或原生scale中，保留其整数编码、零点和存储布局。通过Qwen3-1.7B浮点/GPTQ INT3对的交叉实验，以及Llama-3.2-3B的对照实验（两者校准投影的初始tensor相同但其余9个投影不同），并配合排列扰动控制实验来验证群组级对应关系的重要性。

Result: 在Qwen3-1.7B浮点/INT3对上，双向迁移在新鲜的WikiText和C4语料上保留了自标定文本损失的76.9%-90.5%。每个接收端仍能进一步从自身增益中获益。排列扰动使两个接收端的文本损失均恶化，证明学习到的群组分配在迁移后仍然重要。Llama-3.2-3B对照实验在局部初始tensor一致的情况下，交叉安装保留了98.6%-99.3%的标定收益，同时仍有0.08%-0.13%的perplexity残差偏好接收端自身增益。PIQA任务准确率的读出与文本损失偏好不总是对齐。

Conclusion: 逐群组增益允许将学习到的标定安装到同一预训练模型的对齐表征中，无需接收端训练。群组对齐使安装定义明确，但增益对群组的分配以及周围网络配置都影响迁移质量。迁移保留了大部分文本标定收益，为各节省存储使用接收端现有参数化。

Abstract: Scale calibration learns an update for one model representation. We study how much of that update can be reused by another representation of the same pretrained model. Our transfer procedure extracts positive group-wise gains and installs them in the recipient's weights or native quantization scales without recipient-side optimization. On a quantized recipient, it preserves integer codes, zero points and storage layout. For a Qwen3-1.7B floating-point/GPTQ INT3 pair, bidirectional transfer retains 76.9-90.5% of the text-loss improvement from recipient-specific calibration on fresh WikiText and C4 cohorts excluded from project development. Shuffling the same gain values within each projection worsens both recipients, showing that their learned group assignment matters after transfer. A Llama-3.2-3B control keeps the initial native tensors at all four calibrated projections identical and changes nine projections elsewhere. Cross-installation retains 98.6-99.3% of the text-calibration benefit, alongside a small, resolved preference for each recipient's own gain. These results quantify both the adaptation carried by a reusable calibration update and the remaining benefit of recipient-specific training.

</details>


### [130] [When is a large language model a good calibration agent? Physics-labeled prompting for budgeted engineering simulator calibration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22379)
*Ruo-Qian Wang*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: 本文研究在预算受限的工程仿真器标定中，给大语言模型（LLM）提供物理诊断描述是否比传统无导数优化器更高效。结果表明：物理标注的提示在最初几次评估中带来巨大优势（首次提案的改进率为92% vs 27%，5次评估时误差低21.9倍），但优势在大约15次评估后消失；纯LLM策略因重复提案而停滞；提出一种两阶段混合工作流（LLM预热→在15次评估后交接给Nelder-Mead或GP-BO），该混合策略仅用9次仿真即可达到目标精度，优于纯LLM（12次）和Nelder-Mead（17次）。此外，重复实验揭示了5次评估时LLM运行间变异达9.8倍，敏感性分析表明力统计量仅能识别粘度ν一个参数。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 工程仿真器标定成本高昂，每次仿真需数小时，传统无导数优化器（Nelder-Mead、贝叶斯优化等）将参数视为匿名坐标，丢弃了专家在诊断时使用的可解释物理信息。早期阶段的决策质量决定预算耗尽前能否得到可用标定结果。作者希望检验LLM能否作为标定智能体，将自然语言物理诊断转化为比传统方法更高效的参数提案，特别是在评估次数极少的场景下。

Method: 1) 提出一种物理标注的LLM提案策略（Phys-OPRO）：提示词包含参数边界、历史最佳试验、当前候选的物理诊断文本（如涡脱频率偏低、升振幅偏弱），要求返回JSON格式的参数向量。2) 设计四项提示消融对照（移除诊断、匿名化指标、长度匹配填充、语义错位）。3) 提出两阶段"数值延拓"工作流：LLM提案前15次评估，在固定预算B_switch=15处将累积评估结果交给Nelder-Mead或GP-BO继续优化。4) 两个基准测试：二维圆柱绕流Smagorinsky大涡模拟标定（OpenFOAM，三个参数ν、Ck、Ce，共3047次求解器评估）和随机化阻尼振子反问题（30条轨迹）。5) 多次重复策略（n=25）而非单一轨迹，以统计方式量化LLM解码器变异。6) 统计方法：自助法置信区间、置换检验、Fisher精确检验、配对Wilcoxon符号秩检验。

Result: 主要结果：（1）物理标注在首次提案上的优势——首次改进率92%（23/25）vs 消融组27%（8/30），Fisher p=1.3e-6；（2）5次评估时中位误差低21.9倍（p<10^-4），10次时低4.7倍，15次时差异消失；（3）同一策略在固定种子下重复5次的中位数跨度达9.8倍，确立低预算LLM-优化器比较的分辨率下限；（4）混合GP-BO延拓策略以9次评估达到τ=10^-4，优于纯LLM（12）、消融组（11-14）、Nelder-Mead（17）和GP-BO（>60）；（5）敏感性分析显示力统计量几乎仅识别粘度ν，Smagorinsky系数Ck和Ce事实上无法识别，15次后所有方法进入目标函数的平坦区域。

Conclusion: 物理标注的LLM应被视为预算受限标定中的"预热机制"而非独立优化器。工程指南：在评估预算极为有限的前几次时使用物理诊断选择一个好的起点，当数值历史足以建立可靠响应面后交接给成熟的无导数优化器，并在标定基准上排名优化器之前先检查目标函数实际能识别哪些参数。LLM提案具有9.8倍运行变异性，未来研究应分别报告策略重复次数与种子数。

Abstract: Calibrating expensive engineering simulators requires tuning model parameters to match reference data, a process heavily constrained by computational costs. This study investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs), conditioned on physical diagnostic descriptions of simulation errors, can propose informative parameter updates more efficiently than conventional derivative-free optimizers. We test this on a cylinder-wake Large-Eddy Simulation and a damped-oscillator inverse problem. Physics-labeled prompts are evaluated against four text ablations (removed, anonymized, padded, misdirected) and standard optimizers (Nelder-Mead, Bayesian optimization, CMA-ES, and random search). Results demonstrate a strong early semantic advantage: the first physics-informed LLM proposal improves the initial design in 23 of 25 trials. After five evaluations, the median calibration error is 21.9 times lower than physics-free controls. However, this advantage is transient - disappearing by fifteen evaluations - and inherent LLM decoder variability yields a 9.8-fold performance spread. To address this, we introduce a hybrid workflow that uses the LLM as a warm-start, passing accumulated evaluations to a conventional optimizer. This two-stage numerical continuation policy reaches target accuracy in just 9 simulator runs, outperforming the LLM alone (12 runs), Nelder-Mead (17 runs), and Bayesian optimization (>60 runs). Supported by sensitivity analysis validating the test cases, this hybrid physics-labeled LLM scheme proves highly effective as a calibration agent under strict evaluation budgets.

</details>


### [131] [TRACE: Transformer Residual Activation Codebook Encoding for Communication-efficient Distributed Edge Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22435)
*Muhammad Azlan Qazi,Alexandros Iosifidis,Qi Zhang*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: TRACE提出了一种面向边缘设备分布式Transformer推理的通信高效框架，通过在注意力后的残差激活处插入向量量化器（VQ），并为每个码字预计算下一层的K/V表示，使接收方通过查找表直接恢复跨设备K/V，消除了接收端矩阵乘法计算，并实现通信与计算的重叠。同时通过层次k-medoids聚类构建多分辨率子码本，支持推理时无需重训即可自适应比特率。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 分布式Transformer推理在边缘场景下面临通信瓶颈：序列并行分区间的激活传输主导延迟，且现有压缩方案（如Astra）仍要求接收端在注意力前完成K/V投影计算，造成通信与计算的串行化。Astra的码本比特率在训练时固定，无法适应变化的带宽。

Method: 1) 在每个Transformer层注意力后残差处插入层专属VQ，使用余弦相似度分配和EMA码本更新；2) 后训练校准阶段为每个码字预计算下一层的K/V查找缓冲；3) 推理时仅传输r比特码本索引（带8比特元数据头），接收端通过直接索引查找恢复K/V，与本地MLP/投影并行；4) 通过层次k-medoids对训练后码本聚类，得到(K_0,...,K_R)=(2,4,8,32,1024)的嵌套子码本，实现运行时比特率自适应；5) 提供两种变体：Trace-b（残差后量化，支持缓冲查找和通信-计算重叠）和Trace-nb（残差前量化，精度更高但无法重叠）。训练时引入local-KV dropout（ρ=0.3）防止设备仅依赖本地K/V的退化解。

Result: 在ViT-Base/16（ImageNet-1K、CIFAR-100）和ViViT-B/16（UCF-101）上：Trace-nb相对Astra精度最高提升1.89个百分点；Trace-b精度最高提升1.45个百分点同时端到端推理加速最高1.27倍；通信开销相对未压缩序列并行降低最高22624倍（ViT-Base）和24500倍（ViViT）；在1–20 Mbps带宽范围内均保持通信优势；K-V缓冲预计算节省15.5%–32.3%每设备计算延迟。

Conclusion: 消除接收端对传入数据的计算依赖是分布式Transformer推理降低延迟的关键，多分辨率码本使单一部署模型能灵活适配变化的链路条件。该工作目前限于编码器架构（ViT、ViViT）；扩展到自回归解码器LLM需要因果感知的位置调度策略，留作未来工作。

Abstract: Distributed Transformer inference across co-located edge devices is fundamentally communication-bound, as exchanging activations between sequence-parallel partitions dominates inference latency under commodity edge bandwidths. Existing compression schemes reduce this cost but retain a structural bottleneck: the received data must still undergo key/value projection before attention can proceed, serializing computation behind communication. This paper presents Transformer Residual Activation Codebook Encoding (Trace), a framework that addresses these limitations. Trace places a Vector Quantizer (VQ) at the post-attention residual of every Transformer layer and precomputes codebook-indexed key/value representations. During inference, exchanged activations are encoded into compact codebook indices, allowing receivers to directly recover keys and values through table lookup instead of executing the downstream computations required to derive them. By eliminating the received data downstream computation, Trace enables communication--computation overlap and reduces a key latency bottleneck in distributed Transformer inference. A hierarchical clustering further structures the learned codebook into a multi-resolution hierarchy, enabling runtime adaptation of the communication bitrate without retraining. The framework supports two operating variants: one prioritizing accuracy and the other balancing accuracy and efficiency through buffer-compatible quantization. Experiments on ViT-Base (ImageNet-1K and CIFAR-100) and ViViT-B (UCF-101) show that Trace achieves up to 1.89% higher accuracy and up to 1.27x end-to-end inference speedup compared with the state-of-the-art VQ-based distributed inference framework.
